title: Calibrate a colorimeter on the blank and measure a sealed sample
instruction: Calibrate the colorimeter on the blank and measure the sample at the wavelength on the card, then return both cuvettes to the rack.
context: The blank sets zero absorbance for the cuvette walls and solvent. A wrong reference or ridged faces on the beam gives a plausible but wrong concentration with no warning. The requested wavelength comes from the card. Done by: lab technicians, students. This tests reference-dependent analytical measurement, beyond setting a device value or moving laboratory vessels.
setup: Positions are on the table top, measured forward from the line through the two arm bases and left (+) or right (-) of the midline between them; the arm bases are 610 mm apart. Nothing else is on the table. 1) Colorimeter: a teal ABS plastic housing, 110 mm front to back, 160 mm wide, 65 mm tall, fixed to the table with its centre 168 mm forward and 5 mm right of the midline. Its top has a square sample well, 14.5 mm across and 35 mm deep (floor 30 mm above the table), centred 190 mm forward and 45 mm right; the well's top edges are rounded with a 5 mm radius. Two blue printed triangles, 25 mm in front of and behind the well, mark the light path, which runs front to back. 2) Hood: a navy ABS plastic cover, 55 g, a 32 x 32 mm roof with two 28 mm side skirts, open at the front and back, and a rubber-coated 24 x 18 x 20 mm grip tab on top (tab top 131 mm above the table). It slides front to back on two 4 mm steel rails, 100 mm long, 92 mm above the table, running 10 mm and 80 mm right of the midline on small steel posts. It starts open, its centre 130 mm forward and 45 mm right; sliding it 60 mm forward to the end stop closes it over the well. 3) Buttons: three 16 x 16 x 12 mm polymer push-button caps, 8 g each, on the housing top 55 mm left of the midline, at 132 mm (down arrow, shorter wavelength), 168 mm (up arrow, longer) and 204 mm forward (CAL). Each is sprung (0.75 N at rest, 1.25 N at 2 mm) and registers a press at 2 mm of travel. 4) Indicators, printed or lit on the housing top: four green wavelength lamps labelled 430, 470, 565 and 635 nm, 26 mm left of the midline at 141, 159, 177 and 195 mm forward; a CAL lamp at 204 mm forward, 38 mm left; and a three-digit absorbance display with 10 mm digits centred 128 mm forward, 13 mm left. 5) Rack: a steel cuvette rack, 44 x 164 mm, 24 mm tall, fixed to the table with its centre 190 mm forward and 250 mm right. It has two 15.5 mm square pockets with floors 4 mm above the table: pocket 0 at 190 mm forward, 310 mm right (in front of the right arm), and pocket 1 at 190 mm forward, 190 mm right. 6) Two sealed polystyrene plastic cuvettes, 18 g each: a 12.5 x 12.5 x 45 mm body and a rubber-coated 14 x 14 x 12 mm stopper, 63 mm tall overall. They are physically identical; the blank holds clear water and has a white stopper, the sample holds blue dye and has a blue stopper. On each, two opposite faces are clear and the other two are frosted grey with dark horizontal ridges. Cuvette A stands upright in pocket 0 and cuvette B in pocket 1, square to the table edges. 7) Card: a white paper (cellulose) card, 120 x 80 x 1 mm, taped flat with its centre 180 mm forward and 225 mm left, a blue 6 x 60 mm stripe along its far edge and a three-digit wavelength (24 mm digits) printed on it, readable from the robot's side. The physical objects never move between the 16 layouts; only the number printed on the card, the lit wavelength lamp at the start, which cuvette is the blank and which faces are frosted change (README, Layouts). setup.png and the Dream-1 run show layout 12 (CLI --seed 4): card 635, lamp 635, both cuvettes with frosted faces on the light path as they stand, blank in pocket 1. The scripted demo shows layout 6 (--seed 0): card 470, lamp 565, clear faces already on the light path, blank in pocket 1.
scoring: Released: every gripper TCP >=30 mm from the cuvette bounding box. Still: origin displacement <.5 mm and orientation change <.5 degrees against every observed pose in the preceding .5 s, linear speed <.01 m/s; lid position change <.5 mm over .5 s. Seated: bottom centre <3 mm from the well axis on each lateral axis; lowest bottom corner between well floor-2 mm and floor+2 mm; tilt <=3 degrees. Closed lid: slide within 2 mm of 60 mm. Rack pocket: bottom centre <3.5 mm from pocket centre on each lateral axis, lowest bottom corner between pocket floor-2 mm and floor+2 mm, tilt <=9 degrees (the 12.5 mm body bottomed in the 15.5 mm pocket can lean on a 20 mm wall up to about 8.8 degrees, and that counts as returned); at most one cuvette per pocket, either pocket. Sticky zero: any released cuvette tilt >30 degrees or any cuvette's lowest body corner >5 mm below table, for the rest of the trial. Measurement record: sample seated, released and still, clear-face axis within 10 degrees of the beam axis, current reference at the requested wavelength with log10(I0/Iref) within .02 AU of 0, lid closed and still, valid reading at requested wavelength within .02 AU of (.15,.10,.32,.78 at 430,470,565,635 nm), continuously 1 s; record persists. 0.25: current wavelength is requested and current reference's log10(I0/Iref) is within .02 AU of 0 for that wavelength, or record exists. 0.50: record exists. 0.75: record exists and sample is currently in a rack pocket, released and still. 1.00: record exists and both cuvettes are currently in distinct rack pockets, released and still continuously 1 s. Otherwise 0. Tier conditions are current except the measurement record and sticky zero; highest satisfied tier applies. Success: 1.00 for a further 1 s.
reset_notes: Use zero object jitter. Restore both sealed cuvettes upright at yaw 0 in their numbered pockets, roots 1 mm above the floors; open hood, release all buttons. Choose markings and requested/start wavelength from derived reset seed modulo 16. Clear reference, measurement record, sticky drop and all timers. No liquid is consumed.
fidelity: No optics are simulated: the detector reads I = I0(w) x 10^-A x F for the one seated cuvette under the closed hood, F = 1 with a clear face within 10 degrees of the beam, else 10^-0.6. CAL stores I as the reference; a wavelength change clears it; the display shows log10(Iref/I) or dashes (README, Instrument). Lamps and display are visual only. Layouts change only markings on identical, 4-fold symmetric cuvettes. Cuvettes are rigid sealed bodies.
